newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Copper seen mixed, Chinese said in small-lot deals.
newsitem.headline: Copper seen mixed, Chinese said in small-lot deals.

text.p: Far East base metal dealers had mixed views on Tuesday on the next move in London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices as the markets in Britain and the U.S. re-open after a long holiday weekend.

"I don't think copper will be able to sustain itself above US$2,500 (a tonne)," Vinod Kumar, director of metal company Donald Mcarthy in Singapore, said. "But with the funds playing a major role in the market, it is unpredictable."
"Copper should go down today on a correction. I don't see any strength in the market," another dealer said.
But other dealers believe copper will hold at current levels and may even post some modest gains.
"I think copper will go up. It should remain at these levels unless the funds liquidate," a senior dealer for a European metal trading house in the city-state said.
Another dealer said copper will "consolidate above $2,500 and should stay there for now."

LME brokers Brandeis said in its daily review that good support for three-month copper at around $2,500 a tonne "is preventing prices from aggressively testing the downside" although it sees the market as "seriously overbought."

Three-month copper was seen by the trade at 0230 GMT at $2,515/20 a tonne, slightly easier than the $2,520 close last Friday. Aluminium was quoted at $1,636/40 a tonne against the close on the LME last week at $1,633 a tonne.
Traders said the current high prices for copper have attracted steady Chinese selling of the red metal.
Kumar estimated that Chinese copper sales had reached about 15,000-20,000 tonnes in the last 10 days.
"Prices are still high. They will continue selling," he said. "The Chinese are buying some material and selling it as well."

But a European trader said the selling has not been heavy. "They're certainly buying and selling in bits and pieces," he said. "They can afford to store the copper because they bought it cheaply a few months back."
Another trader said the last thing he heard in the trade was that the Chinese may be buying copper in the market over the next few days.
Copper stocks on the LME are expected to dip by 1,000-1,500 tonnes when the inventories report is released at 0800 GMT.

Regional zinc dealers said they were also checking reports of Chinese material being bought to Singapore. Some 5,000-6,000 tonnes were said to have arrived last week, but dealers doubt if the material will be placed immediately on warrant.

They said between 15,000-20,000 tonnes of zinc remain off warrant here. The volume of zinc in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 11,250 tonnes last Friday, down 250 tonnes from the previous day's report.
Far East traders said they have received no word on the level of aluminium premiums agreed upon for third quarter supply contracts in Japan.
"I think most of the premiums will be set at just below $90 (a tonne). Some were already done at $88," one dealer said.
Another trader said the base of the premiums should be at $87 a tonne, up from the $82-$85 a tonne in the second quarter.
-- Rene Pastor, Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
